bib.title: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023, pages 13003-13051

read.skipped: Per-task scaling plots in Appendix B (figure axis text) and the per-task CoT exemplar prompts in Appendix C were skimmed, not read line by line; the exemplar text is long and is released in the authors' repo.

question: On which BIG-Bench tasks do language models still fall short of the average human rater, and can chain-of-thought prompting close the gap?
hypothesis: Standard answer-only few-shot prompting underestimates model capability on tasks that need multi-step reasoning, which CoT prompting would reveal.
contributions: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH): 23 BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) where no prior reported model beat the average human rater
Manually written 3-shot CoT exemplars for every BBH task, with Codex outputs released
Evaluation of Codex, InstructGPT and PaLM with answer-only vs CoT prompting, and of how the CoT gain depends on scale

method.summary: Filters BIG-Bench from 209 tasks down to 23 hard multiple-choice or exact-match tasks, writes three CoT exemplars per task, and compares few-shot answer-only against CoT prompting on Codex, InstructGPT and PaLM families by greedy decoding and exact match.
method.task: few-shot evaluation of multi-step reasoning on BIG-Bench Hard

datasets.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
datasets.split: random subset of 250 test examples per task, except Causal Judgement (187), Penguins in a Table (146) and Snarks (178), which use all available examples; 3 further examples per task are reserved for few-shot prompting
datasets.source: subset of BIG-Bench (Srivastava et al., 2022); released at github.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard
datasets.preprocessing: Filtered in steps 209 -> 187 (more than three subtasks removed) -> 130 (fewer than 103 examples removed) -> 85 (no human-rater baseline removed) -> 78 (not multiple-choice or exact match removed) -> 36 (best reported model beats average human rater removed) -> 23 (13 tasks judged too hard or out of scope removed). Answer order was randomised for tasks where the first answer was always correct.

models.name: PaLM 8B / 62B / 540B
models.context: input length 2,048 and target length 512 (Appendix B)

models.name: InstructGPT: text-ada-001, text-babbage-001, text-curie-001 (also written text-curie-002 in Section 3), text-davinci-001, text-davinci-002
Codex: code-cushman-001, code-davinci-002 (Section 3 lists code-davinci-002 twice; Figure 4 labels d-1 and d-2 both code-davinci-002)

inference.decoding: greedy decoding (temperature sampling with temperature tau = 0)
inference.max_tokens: OpenAI models: target length 1,000 for Geometric Shapes, 900 for Formal Fallacies, Salient Translation Error Detection and Temporal Sequences, 512 for all other tasks; PaLM: input length 2,048, target length 512
inference.samples: one greedy output per item; no repeats or seeds reported
inference.prompting: 3-shot. Answer-only: task description, exemplar questions with options and answers. CoT: same, with a manually written chain of thought after 'A: Let's think step by step.' in each exemplar, ending 'So the answer is ...'. Both include a task instruction and the answer options in the input.

other.cost_estimate: Footnote 3: evaluating BBH on text-davinci-002 would cost $195.33 USD at $0.02 per 1K tokens, assuming an average prompt length of 1.5K

metrics.name: exact match accuracy
metrics.definition: generated final answer, extracted after 'the answer is', compared with the ground-truth label; multiple-choice options are all shown in the prompt and the model generates the answer (differs from rank/scoring classification)

metrics.name: tasks above average human rater
metrics.definition: count of the 23 tasks on which model accuracy exceeds the BIG-Bench average human-rater score

baselines: Average and maximum human rater (Srivastava et al., 2022)
eval.protocol: Unweighted average over tasks; single run each, no error bars or significance tests.

availability.data: BBH data, prompts and Codex outputs at the same repository

results.claim: Authors attribute CoT failures on Causal Judgement and Ruin Names to missing world knowledge, and on Snarks to models classing both statements neutral and picking an option at random.

limits: Human-rater scores are not representative of human performance; raters had hours per day, could use the Internet, and task formats changed over a year. Beating the average should not be confused with true understanding or reasoning (Section 8.1).
Possible residual label biases despite 250-example subsampling and answer-order randomisation (8.2).
CoT exemplars were hand-written; results may change with their format and wording (8.3).
Almost all tasks are in English (8.4).
Single greedy run, no error bars or significance tests; 250 examples per task makes single-task differences noisy.
Table 2 and Table 3 disagree on PaLM CoT average (65.2 vs 63.3) and best prior result (50.9 vs 52.1).
OpenAI models named are text-davinci-002 and code-davinci-002 and are deprecated; no parameter counts are given for them.
